commit_provenance: Every `commit` below is the commit that was actually compiled and rendered, recorded from the render log rather than re-resolved afterwards. origin/main and claude/figures-missing-and-judged both advanced during this run; the images belong to the earlier commits and the manifest says so.
id_scheme: figure_id is the fragment stem, matching PIXEL-JUDGMENT.md's `fragment` column and NAIVE-MERMAID.json's figure_id. pj_id is PIXEL-JUDGMENT.md's number where the figure has one; figures that exist only on a branch have pj_id null and id_origin says so.
method: Every branch with a commit since 2026-09-01 was diffed against origin/main over whitepaper/figures, website-v2/public/whitepaper/figures and docs/harbor-research/figures. Files the Book's own preamble declares as apparatus rather than drawings (pd-figure-language and its edition overrides, pd-pedagogy, pd-palette, pd-hyperlinks, pd-cite-shortforms, pd-discharges, pd-textbook-map) are excluded by the same rule figure-gates uses. Each surviving variant was compiled through the repository's own build path - skills/harbor-chartwork/scripts/compile_fragment.sh --preamble book - with that branch's whole figure tree and Book preamble materialised first, so a variant whose branch also changed the figure language is rendered under its own figure language. Rendered at 150 dpi (the project's page-scale standard), trimmed to inked content, capped at 1100 px wide, saved as WebP q82.
render_toolchain: xelatex (TeX Live) via a local shim standing in for tectonic, which is not installed here; compile_fragment.sh itself is used unmodified. PDFs rasterised with PyMuPDF + Pillow.

field_notes.variant_count: how many versions of this figure exist (main plus each branch that changed it).
field_notes.claim: what the branch said it was fixing, quoted from its PR body or commit message.
field_notes.claim_is_figure_specific: true when the branch argued about THIS figure by name; false when the quote is the branch-level argument.
field_notes.compiled: true if the variant compiled clean under the Book preamble here.
field_notes.png: repo-relative path to the rendered variant image.

same_slot_rivalries.slot: chapter 7, the claim-signalling discount-factor threshold (register row ch7-30 / §7.7.4)
same_slot_rivalries.fact: delta*(k=3) ~ 0.3425 against the grim-trigger bound 1/3 - a gap of 0.0092

rivals.form: two-curve xy plot: the deviator's payoff against delta, zero line as the indifference reference
delta*(k) against rounds of punishment k, showing how fast the premium falls

same_slot_rivalries.note: Two branches independently drew the SAME chapter-7 fact under two different figure names, so no filename collision flags them. They disagree on form (payoff-vs-delta versus threshold-vs-k) and on the arithmetic: #10190's fragment comment states the gap is 0.0091747, 'i.e. 0.0092 to four places. The caption said "within 0.009", which is FALSE: 0.00917 exceeds 0.009', while #10198's figure is captioned around 'barely 0.009' / 'costs 0.009 of patience over grim'. Only one of these can go in.

claude/figure-qa-resync.finding: Touches no figure SOURCE at all. Its diff against the merge base is confined to docs/harbor-research/exposition/figures/figcheck/*.json, the generated audit files, blockers.json and library-checks.yml - it re-derives the figure-QA records against the live corpus and adds INK-AUDIT.md. No figure has a second version because of it.

claude/swiss-token-generation.finding: Touches no figure source either. It changes the website's Swiss token components, the mega-volume generator, and commits a rebuilt coordination-papers-mega-volume.pdf. The rebuilt Book PDF means the figures PRINT differently, but every fragment is byte-identical to main, so there is no rival variant to render.

Fixes three defects from the Book's design ledger (5.1, 5.2, 5.6), all factual or rule violations rather than style opinions: **D1:** three captions in Chapters 6-8 name "teal" or "dashed amber" for marks that Part IV's chapter-colour override ... actually renders gold or `pderror` red. **D2:** seventeen figure-scale `text=hhamber` annotation nodes across eight fragments in five chapters moved to `pdinkmuted`, per `figures/pd-palette.tex`'s own stated rule that amber is stripes, dots and display only, never small text (3.71:1 on cream). **D3:** `figures/pd-figure-language.tex` (both twins) gains the missing fourth mark family - `pd danger rule`/`arrow`/`fill`/`datum` - built to the caution family's exact construction but wired to `pderror`. `fig-worked-example.tex` (Chapter 7, printed p.400) drew its minute axis at two different scales on the same axis with no break marked. Re-measuring from the source: the labeled coordinate/minute pairs are `{0/0, 1.0/1, 3.0/3, 7.0/12, 8.0/13, 12.5/24}`, so the 3->12 minute span renders at (7.0-3.0)/(12-3) = 4/9 ~ 0.444 tikz-units/minute and the 13->24 span at (12.5-8.0)/(24-13) = 4.5/11 ~ 0.409 units/minute, versus 1.0 units/minute for the 0->1, 1->3 and 12->13 spans - the two long spans render at 41-44% of the short-span scale, silently, with real tick marks and numeric labels that invite a reader to measure duration directly off the page. Fix chosen: (a) redraw to one uniform scale.

**`fig-worked-example`** - the three lane bands were washes at 5-13 % and effectively invisible; they are now edged and readable, and the figure's three rails read as rails. [and, under trade-offs:] `fig-worked-example` chapter T4 6->8 - the three lane bands now carry the drawn edges `craft-rules` 1.3 requires, and those edges pass *behind* labels that carry their own cream knockout. Optically clean, geometrically overlapping; T4 is a geometric test with no notion of z-order.

`whitepaper/figures/fig-swk-stack-map.tex` was four stacked bands with the relation between them undrawn, and it was the heaviest drawing in the Book by ink fraction - 0.553 against a corpus median of 0.146 over the 56 live fragments, i.e. the top of the range and roughly 3.8x the median. Most of that ink was doing no work: four full-width tinted bands and a solid black `MACHINE FLOOR` bar, which is a solid mass doing a job an edge can do. ... Every inter-layer gap now carries two labelled arrows - `provides` up, `assumes` down - at all four boundaries, not just at the floor. A stack map's whole content is the relation between rungs, and that relation was undrawn. ... One thing the drawing was getting wrong. The old fragment tinted the *coordination* band while the caption named the *substrate*.
